# Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral). Run status: COMPLETED.

## Structure and components

- [statement] Test components separately and end to end: reducing fleet capacity at constant traffic reveals per-instance limits, but does not reproduce the dependency load of increasing total traffic. (high confidence) Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/
- [statement] Exercise gradual ramps, sudden load steps, and the return to nominal load. Caching can change the breaking point, and overloaded components may require load to fall substantially before recovery. Stateful tests must also check correctness. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/
- [statement] Timeouts can waste work already performed, while retries multiply offered load. Retrying at several layers can amplify a backend overload into a self-sustaining cascade, so include actual client retry behavior when evaluating overload protection. (high confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/

## How it works

- [statement] WiredTiger 11.3.1 documents that application threads start performing eviction once cache usage reaches eviction_trigger (default 95%), which throttles application operations and increases operation latency; if eviction threads cannot keep up with demand for cache space, application threads are tasked with eviction, potentially causing latency spikes. Sources: https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html — https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/README.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use gradual ramps and abrupt impulses, then reduce load and measure recovery. Warm caches can hide abrupt-load failures, and removing the triggering change may not end an established cascade. (high confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://slack.engineering/slacks-incident-on-2-22-22/
- [statement] Use application-thread eviction, failed eviction, memory and lock contention together when diagnosing the breaking point. CircleCI’s 2019 incident showed that ticket observations alone failed to explain degradation and that application-level metrics could appear recovered while the primary remained degraded. (medium confidence) — https://discuss.circleci.com/t/postmortem-march-26-april-10-workflow-delay-incidents/30060 · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/README.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Interpret queue growth, timeout storms and health-check failure as possible downstream symptoms. Correlate their onset with resource contention and cache behavior to identify the initiating bottleneck; the final visible failure need not identify its cause. (high confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://discuss.circleci.com/t/postmortem-march-26-april-10-workflow-delay-incidents/30060
- [statement] Exercise real retry behavior and dependency failure under load. Work finished after the client has timed out is wasted, and retries multiply offered load (exponentially across deep call graphs). Randomized backoff keeps retries from synchronizing, but when retries keep an overloaded backend overloaded, recovery requires dramatically reducing or eliminating load until the retries stop. Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ ; https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://slack.engineering/slacks-incident-on-2-22-22/
- [statement] A cache-miss feedback loop can sustain failure: misses increase database reads, overloaded reads time out, cache refill fails, and misses persist. Slack documented this mechanism in its 2022 incident; it is evidence for an application-cache test scenario, not proof of an intrinsic MongoDB eviction defect. (high confidence) — https://slack.engineering/slacks-incident-on-2-22-22/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/nsdi13/nsdi13-final170_update.pdf
- [statement] Measure client-perceived availability and latency alongside server metrics. Separate successful-request latency from rejection latency: cheap failures can make aggregate latency look healthy while useful requests remain slow. (low confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/
- [statement] WiredTiger evicts normally as cache fills (eviction_target default 80%, with application threads joining at eviction_trigger default 95%); application-thread eviction throttles operations and raises latency. Correlating load and client latency with cache occupancy, eviction activity and application-thread eviction is reasonable diagnostics; treating lost progress and falling goodput, rather than high occupancy alone, as the sign of a serious failure is a synthesis not stated in WiredTiger documentation. Sources: https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html — https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/README.md, https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Treat cache-full or application-eviction thresholds as evidence to investigate rather than universal failure limits. The MongoDB development README describes workload-dependent detection using exceeded triggers, progress and application-thread eviction time together; this does not establish behavior for every released version. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/README.md · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html
- [statement] Test components separately, then test the complete dependency path. Record the first resource or progress limit reached; later latency, memory pressure, backend failure, or failed health checks can be secondary symptoms rather than the initiating bottleneck. (high confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/
- [statement] Google's SRE guidance supports using randomized exponential backoff, limiting retries per request, and having overloaded servers reject requests; retries reduce the fraction of useful work the backend performs. Comparing these protections against an unprotected baseline and measuring useful completions, retry volume and recovery is a test-design suggestion, not stated by the source. Sources: https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Increase offered load beyond the goodput plateau. Measure client-visible success within deadlines, latency, rejections and timeouts separately; fast rejection must not make successful-request latency look artificially healthy. (high confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/
- [statement] In Facebook’s 2013 memcache system, repeated invalidation of hot keys caused many readers to take the expensive backend path. Per-key leases limited concurrent regeneration. For a MongoDB-backed application cache, this motivates a hot-key invalidation or cold-cache test; it is not evidence of a native MongoDB lease feature. (medium confidence) — https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/nsdi13/nsdi13-final170_update.pdf · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://slack.engineering/slacks-incident-on-2-22-22/
- [statement] WiredTiger continuously evicts pages to free cache space. When its eviction threads cannot keep up with demand for cache space, application threads are tasked with eviction as well, throttling operations and increasing latency (default trigger 95% of cache). Whether eviction activity alone indicates a self-sustaining death spiral is an interpretive judgment, not stated by WiredTiger documentation. Sources: https://source.wiredtiger.com/develop/eviction.html ; https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html — https://source.wiredtiger.com/develop/eviction.html · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html, https://discuss.circleci.com/t/postmortem-march-26-april-10-workflow-delay-incidents/30060
- [statement] Current manual guidance says low available execution tickets alone do not indicate overload; queued reads and writes are the relevant signal. Do not carry the fixed ticket defaults quoted in the 2019 CircleCI postmortem into a current test baseline. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://discuss.circleci.com/t/postmortem-march-26-april-10-workflow-delay-incidents/30060
- [statement] Increase offered load beyond the capacity knee and plot goodput: successful responses completed before client deadlines. A healthy overload response approaches a plateau; collapsing goodput reveals overload instability even if request throughput stays high. (high confidence) Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ — https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/ · keywords: Breaking-point / overload testing methodology (first bottleneck vs visible symptom, cascading failure, thundering herd, cache-eviction death spiral) · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/
- [statement] Cheap rejection has finite capacity. AWS reports that shedding load is not free, so eventually the server falls prey to Amdahl's law and goodput drops. Artificially raising per-instance load by shrinking the fleet is useful for testing a service in isolation but is not a complete substitute for a full end-to-end load test, which also loads the service's dependencies and can uncover other bottlenecks. Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/
- [statement] Alex Bevilacqua’s incident describes MongoDB 3.0.15 and reports improvement after an upgrade. His June 2018 updates qualify the explanation: cache-management and checkpoint improvements were more likely contributors than the initially suggested write-ahead-log optimization. Treat this as historical diagnostic evidence, not a current-release defect or a controlled attribution. (low confidence) — https://alexbevi.com/blog/2018/05/28/troubleshooting-a-mongodb-performance-issue/
